en.title: Mélenchon launches 2027 presidential campaign with wage and retirement pledges
en.dek: Jean-Luc Mélenchon presented his 2027 manifesto at Le Bourget, pledging a higher minimum wage and retirement at age 60.
facts: Jean-Luc Mélenchon launched his 2027 presidential campaign on 7 November.
He presented his manifesto at Le Bourget, north of Paris.
The manifesto is titled "A Shared Future".
Mélenchon pledged to raise France's minimum wage.
He pledged to restore the retirement age to 60.
Die Zeit reported he presented his program as a presidential candidate.
body: Jean-Luc Mélenchon presented his presidential manifesto at Le Bourget, north of Paris, on 7 November, and France 24 reported the document is titled "A Shared Future". Die Zeit reported he presented his program as a candidate for the presidential election.

The manifesto pledges to raise France's minimum wage, and it pledges to restore the retirement age to 60. France 24 and The Straits Times reported these measures ahead of the event. The Straits Times reported the retirement pledge would set the age at 60.

France 24 reported Mélenchon launched his campaign at the Le Bourget venue, and the outlet said he is running in the 2027 presidential election. The Straits Times reported the pledges before the manifesto presentation. The event took place north of Paris.

The Straits Times reported the minimum wage pledge alongside the retirement plan, and France 24 reported he vowed to lower the retirement age at the campaign launch. Both outlets confirmed the two core economic pledges. The Straits Times said the retirement age would return to 60.

Die Zeit covered the manifesto presentation as part of the 2027 race, and the outlet reported Mélenchon presented his program as a candidate. France 24 said the manifesto title is "A Shared Future". The presentation took place ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

The campaign launch took place on 7 November, and the manifesto presentation occurred at Le Bourget. France 24 reported the event ahead of the 2027 presidential race. The Straits Times reported the pledges on the same day.
en.context: Jean-Luc Mélenchon is a candidate in the 2027 French presidential election. France 24 identified him with the France Unbowed party. He presented his manifesto at Le Bourget, north of Paris.
